chunks: Ahmad ibn Idrees, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man upon whose father there is a debt, and for his father there is a provision. Can he give his father from his zakat to pay off his debt? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, and who is more deserving of it than his own father?'
ai.seo_question: Can a son give his father zakat to pay off his debts?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a father’s debt takes precedence over his general maintenance needs when receiving zakat, emphasizing the principle of 'most deserving' (ahquq). This ruling underscores the unique status of parents in Shia jurisprudence, where filial piety extends to financial relief, distinguishing them from other zakat recipients. The hadith reflects the broader ethical imperative of honoring parents, linking material support to spiritual duty.
